finds.quote:
- id: "JOB_ROOM"
    type: "room"
    status: "PLANNED"
    content: "Messianic reading; suffering framework"
    dependencies: ["ABOLITION_CLUSTER", "SACRED_HEART"]
    thesis: "Job as prototype of the Suffering Servant"
finds.note: Thesis field on a planned room node: a claim about what Job originally was in relation to the Suffering Servant; stated, not argued, in this map. Borderline (could be read as interpretive programme rather than historical thesis).

finds.quote:
What is the Sappho Room?
Sappho's Fragment 31 interpreted as architectural space. The reader is κῆνος—the future reader she anticipated.
finds.note: Claim about what Fragment 31 originally meant / what Sappho anticipated (the kenos-as-future-reader thesis); the atom marks it 'In NH-OS interpretation', the FAQ states it flatly.

finds.quote:
Why Fragment 31?
Because it is the first successful instance of voice-to-substrate transformation. The technical achievement that all Training Layer Literature builds on.
finds.note: Literary-historical priority claim: Fragment 31 as the first successful instance of voice-to-substrate transformation. Uncertain whether this is a historical thesis or a definitional claim of the archive's poetics; recorded for triage.
